_about: Single declaration of the requirements graph (S-63, kernel page requirements-graph). The sensor reads this file; the kernel page explains it for humans. Edges are written in one direction only; the inverse is computed. Each edge is enforced only from the status declared in 'enforced_from' (lesson of SDD_chain_artifacts_check: checking every pair everywhere produced 366 false positives).

file_name._about: MJRP, 2026-10-09: a requirement file is <ID>-<slug>.md (S-31-decide-how-data-reaches-the-screen.md). The ID is the identity (frontmatter `id:` and `aliases: [ID]`); the slug is the English title in lowercase ASCII kebab-case, at most slug_max characters, set at birth and frozen (renaming is explicit: req_file_names.py --reslug). Links and embeds name the whole stem, the ID is the display text: [[S-31-decide-how-data-reaches-the-screen|S-31]]. slug_required/alias_required stay false during the migration; a file with no slug has the ID as its whole stem, so [[S-31]] is the right link to it.

edge_syntax.file_node: YAML frontmatter key in the node's own file: `epic: "[[prd#^EP-01]]"`, lists for many targets
edge_syntax.inline_node: Inline field on the line under the node inside its document: `serves:: [[ROADMAP#^OUT-01]]` (epics in prd.md, releases in ROADMAP.md)
edge_syntax.block_anchor: `^ID` at the end of the paragraph or list item that holds the node (outcomes, releases, observable states); letters, digits and hyphens only

_off_track: valid statuses outside the lifecycle order: never count as reached for enforced_from, never open (MJRP, 2026-10-04 14:28: Deferred joins the rules; 2026-10-13 17:15, ADR-0020 A.6: Cancelled joins it -- a requirement that will not be done, superseded or given up; it keeps its ID and its edges (`epic` is still required, `supersedes` says who replaced it) and, unlike Deferred, never comes back: the return is a new node. It does not count in the progress)

derivation._about: F67 (S-168): each status has ONE source; what derives from it is computed by status_sync.py and written by the pre-commit hook in the same commit. The derivation only moves forward: it never demotes a delivered status, never writes Accepted (the human's acceptance or the independent recheck) and never closes a UAT issue (the human's OK). Epic and release statuses are never stored: whoever shows them computes them from their requirements, so there is nothing to write and no second source.

feature.done_with_open_box: unchanged (a finding of done_feature_complete, never a rewrite: the derivation does not demote)

requirement.source: the features that import it (after their own derivation)
requirement.note: a requirement already In progress only moves to Done; one in Backlog, Prioritized or Ready moves to In progress or Done. A feature in Draft or Ready (nothing ticked) moves nothing.

uat_issue.field: uat.md, the `Status` cell of the row
uat_issue.note: `fixing (Fxx)` becomes `fixed (Fxx)` when Fxx is Done or Accepted (also the old rows whose feature is already Accepted, UAT-312 with F48). `closed` is never derived: it is the human's OK, or the independent recheck on the agent track.

derivation.epic: computed, never stored: from its requirements
derivation.release: computed, never stored: from what is planned_for it
derivation.scope_in_commit: the pre-commit derives only from what the commit touches: a touched feature (its own status, the requirements it imports, the UAT rows fixing it), a touched requirement (from its importers) and every row of a touched uat.md. Drift in nodes the commit does not touch is left to `status_sync.py --check` (never swept into someone else's branch).

release_required._about: ADR-0020 A.5: `planned_for` is optional unless the project's contract turns it on with `mjrp_harness.requirements.release_required: true`; then a requirement must have a release from this status on (a Backlog requirement may still be unplanned). The epic's own `planned_for` satisfies it -- it is a shortcut for all the epic's requirements.

identity._about: ADR-0020 D.3: an ID is unique in the REPOSITORY. A project nested in the repository of another one (its contract is under the git toplevel whose root has another contract) carries `mjrp_harness.id_prefix` (e.g. CC) on every per-project sequence the containing project also uses: the prefix is optional in the patterns of these node types, and the sensor refuses a node ID repeated between the nested project and the root one.

observable_state.note: a situation of the system surface the human sees and judges: a screen state of the judged prototype (info-arch.md, visual surface) or a behavior state (behavior.md, non-visual surface: command output, exit code, generated file, hook block, API response, agent behavior). MJRP, 2026-10-04 14:41: one rule for every requirement, no exemption by project type or by date. A link with a path (apps/<app>/docs/specs/info-arch#^x) resolves in that nested project.

edges.name: contributes_to
edges.note: ADR-0020 A.2: an outcome declares the outcome of ANOTHER roadmap it contributes to (`contributes_to:: [[../../ROADMAP#^OUT-03]]` in its section). The target is always a path relative to the declaring file + #^ID, never a bare ID, and is read only when it is the ROADMAP.md of a project with a contract in the same repository. Resolved: passes. Missing (the block does not exist, the target is the own roadmap, a bare ID, a cycle): error, exit 1. Unreachable (outside the repository, not on disk, not a project's ROADMAP.md): not evaluable, exit 2 -- never green, never read.

edges.name: planned_for
edges.note: on an epic it is a shortcut for all its requirements; the requirement overrides

edges.name: points_to
edges.note: F67, decision of the MJRP (2026-10-26 11:30): on the fast lane the feature starts before the requirement is Ready, and the requirement moves to In progress with it (derivation). When EVERY feature that imports the requirement declares `lane: fast`, the edge is enforced from `enforced_from_fast_lane` -- the retroactive step, before the item closes.

edges.name: imports
edges.note: fin-control, 2026-10-18: a feature imports requirements, and an NFR is a constraint of every feature, so it is not imported -- except by a feature of the tracks in `nfr_tracks` (Fix: the item that pays a place where the NFR is not met, `violates:: [[NFR-xx]]`). That feature may import ONLY NFRs (an engineering feature needs no invented story), or none when it names the constitution article it violates (`violates:: [[constitution#N]]` in its spec) -- but only with `fixes:` (the issue it pays; the card takes its release from there), a `violates::` naming that same NFR or an existing article, and a live NFR (rule fix_nfr_import). An NFR import never counts toward one_open_feature or the release of the feature.

edges.name: supersedes
edges.note: required when a Done requirement changes: the change is a new requirement that supersedes the old one

edges.name: delivered_by
edges.note: the commit that delivered a requirement with no Done feature (meta work, or delivered before the graph); evidence for Done

edges.name: accepted_in
edges.note: the human's acceptance: an entry of uat.md ([[uat#^UAT-xx]]) or of the log ('log YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM'); evidence for Accepted; or, for brownfield work closed before the harness, 'histórico anterior ao harness — regra do MJRP de 2026-10-18' (at least one delivered_by commit exists and none is newer than the contract's first commit; the sensor prints the count)

constraints.text: a requirement is imported by at most one open feature (MJRP, 2026-10-04: requirement -> feature 0..1 open at a time)
a feature imports 1..n requirements; a fix (`solution_type: fix`) with a non-empty `fixes:` imports none -- its requirement is the issue it fixes (PDLC v12, F94)

an NFR is not imported by a product feature; it constrains all of them and is checked in review with constitution.md. The one importer is a feature of `imports.nfr_tracks` (Fix) that pays a violation of it (see fix_nfr_import)

a Fix feature that imports an NFR (or imports nothing and names a constitution article) has a non-empty `fixes:`, a `violates::` outside a code fence naming that same NFR (or an article that exists in docs/specs/constitution.md), and the NFR is live: not Cancelled, not superseded
every REQ of a feature is implemented by at least one TASK of the same feature
all requirements imported by one feature are planned for the same release (when the project declares releases)
every edge target resolves: file, heading or block anchor exists
a Done or Accepted requirement has evidence: a Done or Accepted feature imports it, or delivered_by names a commit that exists (the feature that accepts a requirement leaves it Accepted, CC-ADR-0024)
an Accepted requirement has accepted_in pointing to the human's acceptance (uat.md entry or log entry)

a node (requirement or feature) that became Accepted after 2026-10-19 23:36 came in a commit stamped `Human-accepted: <the feature that imports it | requirements>` with no agent Co-Authored-By: the human's acceptance is the commit his command makes, never a status written by hand (CC-ADR-0024 section 6, step 2 of ADR-0019 section 2); not evaluable without git or in a shallow clone; and an ADR born on the MJRP's route (`**Acceptance**: MJRP`, or no route line and dated from 2026-10-26) became Accepted in a commit stamped `Human-accepted: adr:<ID>`, keeping the route it was born with (CC-ADR-0028); and a cell `OK do humano` of the uat.md that became the MJRP's (the form of `uat_tracks_check._HUMAN_OK`) after the commit that accepted CC-ADR-0029 came in a commit stamped `Human-accepted: issue:UAT-nn` (or the feature that links the issue) with no agent Co-Authored-By; until that ADR is Accepted here the effect judges nothing and the output says so (CC-ADR-0029)

an Accepted feature has an accepted_in that resolves (log entry or uat.md anchor) and every requirement it imports, NFRs apart, is Accepted: the feature and its requirements are accepted together (CC-ADR-0024 section 6)
an In progress requirement has an open feature, or activity in stale_days (a commit on the node or its feature, or a log entry citing it) — time rule, daily pass
the observable state a Ready requirement points to did not change after the requirement was last touched — time rule, daily pass

a Ready requirement that points to a screen state (info-arch.md, nested included) points to a state an approved prototype shows: the state's block ID is in a shows:: line of the record in § Protótipos aprovados. Behavior states are exempt (MJRP, 2026-10-04)

a Done or Accepted feature is complete: no unchecked box (- [ ]) in its tasks.md, whatever the task ID looks like, and every REQ of its spec.md -- even one with a project-style ID such as REQ-F-05 -- has a verified_by (audit of pedroso-incorp, 2026-10-18, point 2). There is no warning phase: the graph check has no severity or date cut, every rule is a finding enforced from its status

WARNING (printed as `aviso`, never a finding, never an exit code): a feature of the Fix track declares in `fixes:` every issue of uat.md that is still open (empty «OK do humano») and whose Status cell cites it (`fixing (Fxx)`, `fixed (Fxx: ...)`). The Delivery station of a Fix feature reads only `fixes:` (CC-ADR-0009 section 1, row 2), so an issue that cites the feature and is not declared lets the board show it «Aceito» while the work is open. Incident: UAT-290 (2026-10-24, F52 shown «Aceito» with UAT-285, 287 and 288 `fixing (F52)`)
requirement files live in the folder their epic declares with folder:: in prd.md (ep-NN-<english-slug>/), NFRs in nfr/; dormant while no epic declares folder:: (S-123, MJRP 2026-10-05)
a requirement file is named <ID>-<slug>.md: the slug is lowercase ASCII kebab-case, at most file_name.slug_max characters; required when file_name.slug_required (MJRP, 2026-10-09)

with file_name.link_form = stem, a link or embed to a requirement names the node's whole file stem ([[S-31-decide-how-data-reaches-the-screen|S-31]]); a bare ID or an outdated slug is flagged (Obsidian resolves file names, not aliases) (MJRP, 2026-10-09)

a Ready requirement that points to a screen state (info-arch.md, nested included) requires docs/specs/design-system.md in the same project as that info-arch.md -- the visual identity is decided before the contract (audit C F10, MJRP 2026-10-09)
a node ID of a project nested in a repository is not repeated in the root project of that repository (ADR-0020 D.3): the nested one carries the contract's id_prefix
a contributes_to target is a relative path + #^ID to an outcome of the ROADMAP.md of another project of the same repository: never a bare ID, never the own roadmap, no cycle (ADR-0020 A.2)
every node has a non-empty `## <lang>` section for each language in `languages` (S-110)

_evidence: S-67 (MJRP, 2026-10-04): status asks for evidence, one rule for every project — the feature for code-app work, the commit for meta work or work delivered before the graph.
_languages: S-110 (MJRP, 2026-10-05 09:39): every requirement and NFR node carries one `## <lang>` section per language, same file, same ID; the contract's mjrp_harness.requirements.languages overrides ([] turns it off)
_tags: MJRP, 2026-10-06: every outcome carries 1 to 3 category tags (`tags:: #a #b` in its ROADMAP section) and every epic inherits the tags of the outcome it serves and may add up to 3 of its own (`tags::` under its heading in prd.md). Free vocabulary: the sensor checks only the format (English kebab-case after #) and the count.
